antidotes.why: The second half of the same answer.
Let the monkey jump; wait and watch.

chains.summary: The mind is restless, strong, and stubborn, as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees that by practice and letting go it is held. Little by little, with understanding held firm, the mind is brought back each time it wanders. To the one whose mind is calm, the highest happiness comes.
chains.title: The mind is hard to hold, and can be trained

verses.m: Arjuna said: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana, I do not see how it can last, because of restlessness.
verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥

verses.m: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verses.sa: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥

verses.m: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥

chains.summary: A mind that follows a wandering sense has its wisdom carried off. As wind carries a boat on water, a striving, wise person is pulled this way.
chains.title: The boat and the wind

verses.m: The turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise person who is striving, Arjuna.
verses.sa: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥

verses.m: When the mind runs after the roving senses, it carries away one's understanding, as the wind carries a boat away on the water.
verses.sa: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥

chains.summary: The self is the rider, the body is the chariot, the intellect is the driver, the mind is the reins, and the senses are the horses. Without understanding and with the mind unyoked, the senses run like bad horses and the goal is missed. With understanding and a yoked mind, the senses obey and the journey's end is reached.
chains.title: The chariot

verses.m: Know the self as the rider, the body as the chariot, the intellect as the charioteer and the mind as the reins. The senses, they say, are the horses, and the things of the world are the roads they run on.
verses.sa: आत्मानँ रथितं विद्धि शरीरँ रथमेव तु । बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च ॥ इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुर्विषयांस्तेषु गोचरान् । आत्मेन्द्रिय मनोयुक्त भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः ॥

verses.m: For one who lacks understanding, whose mind is never held steady, the senses run out of control like a driver's wild horses. For one who has understanding, whose mind is always steady, the senses obey like good horses.
verses.sa: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ॥

chains.summary: Anger is the enemy hardest to defeat. Greed is the illness without end. The mind is faster than the wind. Worries outnumber the blades of grass.
chains.title: The enemy and the illness

verses.m: Yaksha: 'Which enemy is hardest to conquer? Which disease has no end? Who is considered good, and who is not?' Yudhishthira: 'Anger is the enemy hardest to conquer; greed is the disease without end; one who wants the good of all beings is good; one without compassion is not.'
verses.sa: कः शत्रुर्दुर्जयः पुंसां कश्चव्याधिरनन्तकः / कीदृशश्च स्मृतः साधुरसाधुः कीदृशः स्मृतः क्रोधः सुदुर्जयः शत्रुर्लोभोव्याधिरनन्तकः / सर्वभूतहितः साधुरसाधुर्निर्दयः स्मृतः

verses.m: Yaksha: 'What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than blades of grass?' Yudhishthira: 'A mother is heavier than the earth; a father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; worries are more numerous than blades of grass.'
verses.sa: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा / मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्

depicts.m: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
depicts.sa: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
depicts.why: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn.

depicts.m: You plunge into the underworld, leap across the sky, wander round every direction, O mind, out of restlessness. Why do you never, even by mistake, remember that pure Brahman, your own Self, by which you would find peace?
depicts.sa: पातालमाविशसि यासि नभो विलङ्घ्य दिङ्मण्डलं भ्रमसि मानस चापलेन । भ्रान्त्यापि जातु विमलं कथमात्मनीनं न ब्रह्म संस्मरसि निर्वृतिमेषि येन ॥
depicts.why: Depicts a mind that has been everywhere.

depicts.m: Yaksha: 'What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than blades of grass?' Yudhishthira: 'A mother is heavier than the earth; a father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; worries are more numerous than blades of grass.'
depicts.sa: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा / मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्
depicts.why: Shows the mind outrunning the wind.

depicts.m: Dhritarashtra: 'Everything is always unsettled, and this mind is always unsettled. Wise one, tell me of the state that is free from unrest.' Vidura: 'I see no peace for you apart from learning and discipline, apart from mastering the senses, apart from giving up greed.'
depicts.sa: नित्योद्विग्नमिदं सर्वं नित्योद्विग्रमिदं मनः / यत्तत्पदमनुद्विग्नं तन्मे वद महामते नान्यत्र विद्यातपसो नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात् / नान्यत्र लोभसन्त्यागाच्छान्तिं पश्यामि तेऽनघ

depicts.m: Where else will my mind find happiness? Like the bird on a ship at sea that flies off and comes back to the ship again.
depicts.sa: मेरो मन अनत कहाँ सुख पावे । जैसे उड़ि जहाज को पच्छी, फिरि जहाज पर आये ॥
depicts.why: Shows the mind flies off and finds nowhere to land.

depicts.m: As a bird tied by a string flies in every direction and, finding no resting place anywhere else, settles down at the very place it is tied, so, dear one, the mind flies in every direction and, finding no resting place anywhere else, settles down on the breath; for the mind is tied to the breath.
depicts.sa: स यथा शकुनिः सूत्रेण प्रबद्धो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनमलब्ध्वा बन्धनमेवोपश्रयत एवमेव खलु सोम्य तन्मनो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनमलब्ध्वा प्राणमेवोपश्रयते प्राणबन्धनꣳ हि सोम्य मन इति ॥
depicts.why: Shows a tethered bird flying every way and finding no perch.

depicts.m: The mind runs here and there, restless and pointless; it wanders far away, like a dog in a village.
depicts.sa: इतश्चेतश्च सुव्यग्रं व्यर्थमेवाभिधावति । मनो दूरतरं याति ग्रामे कौलेयको यथा ॥
depicts.why: A seeker describes his own mind running everywhere for nothing.

depicts.m: Harder than drinking up the ocean, harder than uprooting Mount Meru, harder even than swallowing fire, is the mastery of the mind.
depicts.why: Depicts the speaker finding his mind harder than any feat.

gloss: The mind that will not stay. Arjuna's own words: cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa, as hard to hold as the wind. This is the inner state of cāñcalya, the restless mind.

heals.m: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, from there one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the self.
heals.sa: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
heals.why: Shows wandering is expected and the practice is only the returning.

heals.m: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
heals.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
heals.why: The teacher names two things that hold the hard mind.

heals.sa: Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch.
heals.why: Shows the monkey is allowed to jump and one's job is only to watch.

heals.m: If you set the body apart and rest in awareness, then this very moment you will be happy, at peace and free of bondage.
heals.sa: यदि देहं पृथक् कृत्य चिति विश्राम्य तिष्ठसि । अधुनैव सुखी शान्तो बन्धमुक्तो भविष्यसि ॥
heals.why: Shows resting in awareness offered as a place the restless mind can stop.

heals.m: Do not stir your mind with yes and no, with plans and doubts. Be still, and rest happily in your own joyful Self.
heals.sa: मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय । उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
heals.why: Shows sankalpa and vikalpa, the to and fro of the mind, are what is set down.

heals.m: The calm mind does not run off to crowded places or to the forest. Whatever and wherever, it stays the same.
heals.sa: न धावति जनाकीर्णं नारण्यमुपशान्तधीः । यथातथा यत्रतत्र सम एवावतिष्ठते ॥
heals.why: Shows the urge to change place to feel better.

heals.m: When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs on every side, a person withdraws the senses from their objects, his wisdom is firmly set.
heals.sa: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
heals.why: Shows a way to pull attention back from what scatters it.

heals.m: You plunge into the underworld, leap across the sky, wander round every direction, O mind, out of restlessness. Why do you never, even by mistake, remember that pure Brahman, your own Self, by which you would find peace?
heals.sa: पातालमाविशसि यासि नभो विलङ्घ्य दिङ्मण्डलं भ्रमसि मानस चापलेन । भ्रान्त्यापि जातु विमलं कथमात्मनीनं न ब्रह्म संस्मरसि निर्वृतिमेषि येन ॥
heals.why: Locates rest in the one place it has not looked.

hero.m: When the mind runs after the roving senses, it carries away one's understanding, as the wind carries a boat away on the water.
hero.sa: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥

loci.m: When the mind runs after the roving senses, it carries away one's understanding, as the wind carries a boat away on the water.
loci.sa: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥

practices.m: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
practices.why: Bearing what passes without being moved.

practices.m: When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs on every side, a person withdraws the senses from their objects, his wisdom is firmly set.
practices.sa: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
practices.why: Shows wisdom staying set when the senses are gathered.

practices.m: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
practices.sa: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
practices.why: Cultivates the capacity to hold steady while the surge passes.

practices.m: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
practices.sa: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥

practices.m: When pain of body or mind arrives and nothing can be done about it, do not keep thinking about it. Not dwelling on it is the medicine for sorrow; brooding does not make it leave, it only makes it grow.
practices.sa: भैषज्यमेतद्दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् / चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते / यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुचिन्तयेत्
practices.why: Shows withholding attention from the loop as the practice.

practices.m: If an undertaking fails, do not torment yourself over it. Keep applying yourself again and again; this is the highest rule for those who lead.
practices.sa: विपन्ने च समारम्भे सन्तापं मा स्म वै कृथाः / घटेतैवं सदाऽऽत्मानं राज्ञामेष परो नयः

practices.m: Never give up what is right out of desire, rage or hatred. Don't be overjoyed by what pleases you, nor burn with distress at what does not.
practices.sa: न च कामान्न संरम्भान्न द्वेषाद्धर्ममुत्सृजेत् / प्रिये नातिभृशं हृष्येदप्रिये न च संज्वरेत्
practices.why: Holding to dharma under pull is shown.

practices.m: "Child, keep courage in your heart, and do what this moment asks of you today." Hearing his teacher, Bharat rose and had everything made ready.
practices.sa: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥
practices.why: Shows courage held in the heart while the hands work.

stories.l: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.
stories.s: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.

stories.l: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.
stories.s: Yama pictures a person as a chariot: the self is the rider, the body the chariot, the intellect the driver, the mind the reins and the senses the horses. With a steady mind the horses obey; without it they bolt. He ends with the call to arise and wake.

stories.l: Steadiness is proved when neither neglect nor luxury moves you.
stories.s: Young Shuka, already wise, is sent by his father Vyasa to King Janaka. Janaka ignores him at the gate for seven days, then lets him wait in the courtyard seven more, then surrounds him with luxury for seven days. Shuka stays exactly the same throughout, and Janaka bows to him.

stories.l: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.
stories.s: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
stories.t: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
